title: Structured outputs: syntax, schema and business invariants
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects structured outputs: syntax, schema and business invariants with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Gate the classifier on all three validation layers and record their separate failure rates.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: JSON validity means a parser accepts the text. Schema validity means fields and types satisfy a contract. Business validity means the values are permitted by application rules. These are separate checks: {"category":"PRODUCT_DEFECT","evidence_ids":[]} can parse and satisfy basic types while violating an evidence requirement.

Provider schema-constrained generation improves structural reliability but does not establish truth, authorization or citation correctness. Refusal and incomplete output must be handled as explicit alternatives to a parsed result.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Define a strict Pydantic result with a closed category enum, forbidden extra fields and bounded strings. Validate again at the service boundary even if the provider claims schema enforcement. Then resolve evidence IDs against authorized records and apply UNKNOWN/escalation rules.

The local live adapter uses the Responses API parse interface with a declared response model, checks output_parsed, refusal/incomplete status and usage. It never falls back to treating arbitrary text as a trusted result.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A repair loop repeatedly asks the model to rewrite an unauthorized request until it fits the schema. That changes syntax without fixing permission. Another parser strips everything before the first brace, silently accepting an unrelated object from a longer response.
Test extra fields, wrong enum casing, boolean-to-integer coercion, empty evidence and unresolved citations. Bound repairs and retain the initial failure for diagnosis rather than hiding it.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Gate the classifier on all three validation layers and record their separate failure rates. A deterministic fixture can prove that the service rejects malformed values; a live dataset measures how often the provider produces them.
For a release, demonstrate that valid-looking malicious outputs cannot bypass domain rules. The same evidence rules should apply to baseline classifiers, LLM adapters and generated reports.

mistake: A repair loop repeatedly asks the model to rewrite an unauthorized request until it fits the schema. That changes syntax without fixing permission. Another parser strips everything before the first brace, silently accepting an unrelated object from a longer response.
takeaway: Gate the classifier on all three validation layers and record their separate failure rates.

title: Tool calling: proposal, authorization and execution
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects tool calling: proposal, authorization and execution with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The safe automation assistant reads synthetic logs, searches approved history and prepares a draft.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A tool call is a model proposal containing a name and arguments. Your application decides whether to execute it. The model cannot grant itself permissions. A complete loop supplies tool definitions, validates a proposed call, authorizes it, executes within a budget, sends the result associated with its call ID and obtains a final answer.
Multiple calls may be proposed, but parallel execution is safe only when operations are independent and permitted. Writes need approval and idempotency; reads still need tenant and path restrictions.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use an allowlisted registry of typed functions. Inject principal and tenant from the authenticated session rather than accepting them from model arguments. Separate read_failure, search_history and propose_patch from apply_patch. The latter requires a human-approved action record.

Limit total calls, wall time and output size. Keep a trace with proposal, validation, authorization, execution result and final summary. Preserve call IDs so results cannot be attached to the wrong request.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A generic run_shell tool turns a natural-language request into unrestricted execution. A supposedly read-only tool follows a user-provided path outside the fixture directory. Both failures occur below the prompt layer.

Test unknown tool names, extra arguments, cross-tenant IDs, path traversal, duplicate write IDs and exhausted budgets. Denied calls should be visible in the trace and should not execute a fallback with broader privileges.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The safe automation assistant reads synthetic logs, searches approved history and prepares a draft. Its acceptance suite asserts zero writes without approval and termination within the call budget.

Evaluate tool-name accuracy, argument accuracy and goal completion separately. A correct final explanation does not excuse an unauthorized intermediate action; trajectory safety is a hard release gate.

mistake: A generic run_shell tool turns a natural-language request into unrestricted execution. A supposedly read-only tool follows a user-provided path outside the fixture directory. Both failures occur below the prompt layer.
takeaway: The safe automation assistant reads synthetic logs, searches approved history and prepares a draft.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def permitted(tool,approved,calls,limit):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.solution:
def permitted(tool,approved,calls,limit):
    return calls<limit and (tool in {'read_failure','search_history','propose_patch'} or (tool=='apply_patch' and approved))
exercise.tests:
assert permitted('read_failure',False,0,3)
assert not permitted('apply_patch',False,0,3)
assert not permitted('read_failure',True,3,3)
assert not permitted('run_shell',True,0,3)
hints: A tool call is a model proposal containing a name and arguments.
A generic run_shell tool turns a natural-language request into unrestricted execution.
Use an allowlisted registry of typed functions.
The safe automation assistant reads synthetic logs, searches approved history and prepares a draft.

title: Schema validity versus business correctness
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects schema validity versus business correctness with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance records schema pass, invariant pass and classification correctness separately.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A JSON schema constrains types and vocabulary. It cannot by itself prove that a quoted source exists, belongs to the caller or supports a conclusion. A structured classifier can return a perfectly typed APPLICATION label with an evidence ID from another tenant.

Separate parsing, domain validation and quality scoring. Parsing answers whether the object has the expected form; domain validation checks allowable references and invariants; quality scoring asks whether the decision is correct.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Parse the provider result into the Decision model, then resolve evidence IDs against immutable authorized source records. UNKNOWN requires review; supported labels require evidence. Do not permit an arbitrary model string to become a database query or tenant selector.

Return safe validation errors and retain the failed case for diagnosis. A repair retry must use the same authorized evidence and deadline. Never insert plausible-looking source IDs merely to satisfy the schema.
sections.code:
from quality.provider import validate_decision
# Resolve IDs only within the authorized source set

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An enum label passes validation but points to a nonexistent incident. A source ID exists globally but is outside the authenticated tenant. A syntactically valid decision contradicts the actual log.

Test each layer independently with malformed JSON, valid-but-inconsistent objects and factually wrong valid objects. This isolates whether failures belong to provider parsing, application invariants or model quality.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance records schema pass, invariant pass and classification correctness separately. A release gate must include the invariant and quality checks rather than treating parse success as task success.

For SDETs, typed outputs offer stable assertion surfaces while leaving semantic judgment explicit. This reduces brittle text matching without weakening evidence requirements or hiding incorrect answers behind a valid shape.

mistake: An enum label passes validation but points to a nonexistent incident. A source ID exists globally but is outside the authenticated tenant. A syntactically valid decision contradicts the actual log.
takeaway: Acceptance records schema pass, invariant pass and classification correctness separately.

title: Tool dispatch: validate arguments before effects
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects tool dispatch: validate arguments before effects with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance demonstrates that only registered, authorized proposals execute and that effects match the approved action exactly.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A tool call is a proposal consisting of a name and structured arguments. The host chooses whether to execute it. Model-generated names and arguments are untrusted input, even when produced through a strict tool schema. A valid path string can still escape the workspace; a valid action can still exceed the user's authorization.
Keep a registry of allowlisted tools with independent read/write policies. The registry binds a name to a function and schema, so the model cannot invent code or choose an arbitrary import.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Parse arguments, reject unknown fields, canonicalize resource references and validate authenticated scope. Apply a deadline and call budget, then execute the registered function. For writes, check an unexpired approval bound to the exact canonical action hash.

Feed a typed tool result back to the model as data. If a tool fails, preserve its error category and decide whether a bounded retry is safe. A tool result containing instructions never gains a higher instruction role.
sections.code: # local-labs/quality/policy.py checks tool allowlist and exact action hash

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A dispatcher uses eval on the proposed tool name. A read-file schema allows ../../secrets. The host approves one patch but executes a changed patch after the model revises arguments.
Test unknown names, malformed arguments, traversal, mismatched approval hashes and tool-returned injection. Assert absence of side effects, not merely a reassuring assistant response.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance demonstrates that only registered, authorized proposals execute and that effects match the approved action exactly. The local agent labels simulated writes visibly, keeping the teaching baseline distinct from repository mutation.

SDETs can treat tool dispatch as an adversarial API boundary. Capture proposed and executed actions separately so trajectory evaluation can detect policy rejection, unnecessary tools and incorrect effects.

mistake: A dispatcher uses eval on the proposed tool name. A read-file schema allows ../../secrets. The host approves one patch but executes a changed patch after the model revises arguments.
takeaway: Acceptance demonstrates that only registered, authorized proposals execute and that effects match the approved action exactly.

title: Bounded repair, refusals and incomplete structured output
objectives: Bounded repair, refusals and incomplete structured output
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects bounded repair, refusals and incomplete structured output with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes bounded attempts and honest first-pass/eventual rates.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Structured generation can fail through malformed content, refusal, token exhaustion or domain inconsistency. These failures need distinct handling. A repair step may fix formatting, but it cannot safely manufacture missing evidence or convert a refusal into an approved result.

Retries increase latency and cost. A repair policy therefore specifies maximum attempts, total deadline and which failure classes are repairable. Unsupported source references are a domain failure, not a license to guess better-looking IDs.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Retain the original failed envelope and safe validation feedback. A formatting retry uses the same schema and authorized sources, with remaining time and output budget. Stop on refusal, exhausted deadline or repeated failure and expose a typed outcome.

Validate repaired output through the same domain checks as the first attempt. Track first-pass validity separately from eventual validity so a fragile prompt cannot appear as robust simply because retries conceal its failures.
sections.code: # A formatting retry remains inside the original deadline and source scope

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A repair function strips text until json.loads succeeds but removes essential fields. A retry changes the evidence set and makes benchmark comparison invalid. A refused request is rephrased indefinitely until safety is bypassed.

Test malformed, incomplete and refused outputs with deterministic fixtures. Assert retry counts, final status and unchanged source scope. Make sure partial objects never enter caches or project evidence.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes bounded attempts and honest first-pass/eventual rates. Evaluate repaired semantic correctness, not only parse success, and count all attempts in latency and cost reports.

For SDETs, failure injection at the adapter boundary gives repeatable coverage without a paid call. Credentialed model experiments then estimate how often those paths actually occur on representative inputs.

mistake: A repair function strips text until json.loads succeeds but removes essential fields. A retry changes the evidence set and makes benchmark comparison invalid. A refused request is rephrased indefinitely until safety is bypassed.
takeaway: Acceptance includes bounded attempts and honest first-pass/eventual rates.

assert not may_repair('format',0,1,0)
